title: The Primary Source
logline: Loretta Stinson writes a memoir full of breezy, contradictory stories, and the chapter titled 'My Favorite Son' still has a blank where the name goes. Barney hires a ruthless fact-checker and goes to war with James over the blank, while the gang lobbies Loretta for better versions of themselves and finds out exactly who her source was.
coldOpen: Kids, in the spring of 2013, your Uncle Barney's mother published her memoir. By published, I mean two hundred copies from a copy shop, read aloud at brunch.

couch.line: It was three hundred pages long. Barney disputed three hundred and four of them.

guests.name: Greta Voss
guests.role: the most feared fact-checker in New York publishing; thirty-one years at a magazine, needs two sources for everything including small talk, and answers almost every claim with 'Source?' and 'Unverified.'

scenes.summary: Hockey night on Barney's 300-inch TV. Loretta arrives with her memoir, Mostly True. Barney's birthplace has changed again, chapter nine is 'My Favorite Son, TK', and chapter twelve puts the whole gang in it, unflatteringly. Barney vows to fact-check it and win the chapter; Robin tells him to pick one.

beats.line: Ted. On this TV, I can count the goalie's fillings.
I can see the referee's soul, Robin. He's so tired.
Three hundred inches. When somebody gets checked into the boards, my neighbors file an insurance claim.
Hello, sweeties! Don't get up. I've written a memoir.
A what?
A memoir, sweetie. It's called Mostly True. My book club is printing two hundred copies.
Smart title. Legally.
Mom. What's in it?
My life, sweetie. My travels, my men, my boys. Mostly the men.
Page one. Barney was born at a Hall and Oates concert.
Mom, last Christmas you told me I was born in an elevator.
That was the Christmas version, sweetie.
There's a Christmas version?
There's one for every holiday. The Arbor Day version has a canoe.
Chapter nine. My favorite son, TK.
beats.title: Mostly True: Contents

beats.line: Who's TK?
Newsroom shorthand. It means to come. She hasn't picked yet.
You haven't picked? You've had thirty-eight years!
It's very close, sweetie. James sent soup on Tuesday.
Wait. Chapter twelve, Barney's friends? We're in it?
All four of you, honey! I've met you at every Thanksgiving.
Ted, a tall boy who explained a doorknob to me for forty-five minutes.
That's not fair. It was a Victorian doorknob, and it was riveting.
What does mine say?
Marshall, a large, gentle man who cried at my microwave.
Loretta, that is wildly out of context.
Lily, the sweetest little kindergarten teacher.
Sweet? I made three dads cry at parent-teacher night. On purpose.
Do I want to know?
Robin, a lovely Canadian girl. Barney showed me her music video.
How many copies did you say?
Two hundred, honey. They print Thursday.
Great. That's a manageable number of fires.
Mom, I am hiring a fact-checker.
Wonderful, sweetie. The reading's Sunday brunch. Bring your friends, they're very popular in chapter twelve.
Nobody panic. By Sunday, that book will be completely accurate, and I'll be her favorite.
Pick one.

scenes.summary: Greta the fact-checker finds Barney's claims unverifiable and his birth certificate says taxicab. James arrives with Loretta as a primary source; the suit-origin flashback reveals the brothers shared one suit and James coined 'Suit up'. Loretta will pick her favorite by Sunday, and the brothers start bidding. Alone, Greta flags page ninety-one: 'I wasn't much of a mother.' Barney keeps that one for himself, then turns Greta's own runner on her.

beats.line: The next morning, Barney hired the most feared fact-checker in New York publishing.
Greta Voss. Thirty-one years at a magazine. One comma got past me. I still think about it.
Greta, my mother's book contains forty-one lies about me. Page six.
Barney cried at his first haircut. I did not cry. I was mourning. Those curls were legendary.
Source?
Me.
Unverified.
Also, I pulled your birth certificate. Place of birth: a taxicab.
A concert, an elevator, a taxi. Even the State of New York can't keep her story straight.
Morning, little brother. I heard you hired a fact-checker. So I brought a primary source.
A primary source.
This is about chapter nine, isn't it?
I'm not here to fight. I'm here to accept the favorite son title. Graciously.
Greta, page forty. Who's the original suit man in this family?
Me. I've worn a suit every day since I was seven.
Every other day.
Oh, it was one suit, sweetie. The boys took turns.
That is a complete and total—
Kids, here's how Loretta remembered it.
One suit, boys. It was on sale. You're sharing.
I'll take Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
What do I get?
Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, sweetie.
And Sunday?
On Sunday, the suit rests.
Here, little brother. It's Tuesday. Suit up.
Suit... up.
That never happened. I invented suit up.
Two sources against one. It stands.
They're related!
So are you.
So, Mom. I'm the original.
The original? You're the rough draft.
Boys, boys. I'll decide by Sunday. Best son by brunch gets chapter nine.
Mom, I gave you two grandchildren.
I gave you a life-size Stormtrooper.
He's lovely company. He never asks where I've been.
I'll take you to brunch every Sunday.
I'll take you to brunch every Sunday. On my yacht.
You have a yacht?
Greta?
Unverified.
Bye, sweeties! May the best son win.
One more item. Page ninety-one.
I wasn't much of a mother. The boys turned out wonderful anyway.
Do you dispute it?
Leave that one with me.
Fine. Also, your welcome mat just texted you my weight. It's wrong.
Source?
Me.
Unverified.

scenes.summary: Lily invites Loretta for tea to lobby her; Ted, Marshall and Robin ambush the visit one at a time with their own pitches. Loretta reveals chapter twelve came from Barney, who calls her every Sunday to talk about them. Marshall secretly lobbies for 'angelic' on Lily's behalf.

beats.line: Meanwhile, Lily had invited Loretta over for a friendly cup of tea.
Dad. Was it a bribe?
Your Aunt Lily prefers the term hospitality with conditions.
More cookies, Loretta? I baked them myself.
Oh, honey. That's so sweet.
Not sweet. Nothing about me is sweet. These cookies are a bribe.
For chapter twelve, I'd like: Lily Aldrin. Children fear her. Parents fear her more.
That's adorable. I'll make a note.
Loretta! What a coincidence. I just happen to have nine pages of notes.
Ted. You can't ambush my ambush.
Mostly footnotes. And a short essay on the Victorian doorknob. With diagrams.
Sweetie, the whole book is only three hundred pages.
Then this will really stand out.
Loretta, I made you my mom's tater tot hotdish. For no reason. Unrelated to the microwave.
But since you brought it up. It had a button that just said potato.
Somebody at that factory believed in potatoes, Loretta. I was moved.
Loretta. Robin. Let's talk numbers.
Cut the music video, and I put your book on the morning news.
Oh, I could never cut that, honey. My book club read it twice.
I know where the copy shop is, Loretta.
How do you even remember all this stuff about us?
I don't, sweetie. Barney tells me. Every Sunday, on the phone.
Barney calls his mother every Sunday?
Six a.m. sharp. He says it's the only hour no woman is awake.
So the doorknob thing came from Barney. He thinks I'm boring.
He said it was the most boring hour of his life. Then he asked if you'd do it again this year.
Did he tell you about the microwave?
He cried telling it.
See? That potato button gets everybody!
And the music video?
Oh, he plays it while I'm on hold.
Great. I'm hold music.
Thank you for the tea, sweet Lily.
Terrifying Lily.
Loretta. For Lily, could you maybe write angelic?
Noted, sweetie.
What did you just whisper to her?
Hotdish reheating instructions!

scenes.summary: The brunch reading at Café Lavallière. Robin finds her section moved to the sign. Loretta reads chapter twelve with everyone's lobbying merged. At chapter nine, James makes his closing argument; Barney withdraws and asks her to change page ninety-one instead, because it's the only untrue thing in the book. Greta verifies him. Loretta names her favorite son: Tom. Future Ted reveals every birth story was true.

beats.line: I asked her to take it out of the book. She took it out of the book.
beats.title: Brunch Reading Today

beats.line: Welcome, book club! Chapter twelve. Barney's friends.
Ted Mosby, architect, sent nine pages of notes. They're the appendix now. It's longer than my second divorce.
The doorknob essay made it in?
Every word, sweetie. The book club skipped it as a group.
Marshall cried at my microwave. He would like you to know it had a potato button.
Thank you, Loretta. History will understand.
Lily. One source said terrifying. Another said angelic. So: Lily Aldrin, a terrifying angel.
Who said angelic?
An anonymous source.
Unverified.
And Robin, as promised, you're not in the book.
I'm on the sign, Loretta. Outside. It's laminated.
And now. Chapter nine. My favorite son.
Mom, a closing statement. I gave you grandchildren. I gave you Tom. I gave this family suit up.
Mom.
I withdraw.
Leave chapter nine blank. Change page ninety-one.
Ninety-one? Oh, sweetie, that one's true.
We had one suit, and you made it sound like a tradition.
You told me I was born at a concert, so I grew up thinking I was the headliner.
That page is the only thing in your book that isn't true.
Source?
Me.
Verified.
I just told you boys whichever story you needed that night.
I know, Mom. They all worked.
He's right, Mom. Change ninety-one.
All right. Then I've decided. My favorite son is...
Tom.
My husband?
He sends flowers. And he's never once hired a fact-checker.
Mom!
Kids, Greta kept digging for nine more years. Loretta went into labor at a Hall and Oates concert.
She got stuck in the elevator, and she had Barney in a cab. Every version was true.
As your Uncle Barney still puts it, most people are born in one place. He was born on tour.
